title: Mounting bracket and hardware need fixing first. But the rack is great
text:
Mounting bracket and hardware need fixing first. But the rack is great. The holes in the mounting bracket are placed in such a way that only one side attaches to a stud in the wall. The holes are wide enough apart that you would need a second stud in the wall next to it. So if you have the wall open or it is new construction, you are in luck. If you can remove a vertical strip of drywall/sheetrock and add in another 2x4 (even a shorter one) it would help a LOT.

I you can't, then figure out which direction side to side you will most often want to use the rack and mount the OTHER side into the stud. Do NOT use the provided anchors in the stud. (some are for masonry and some for drywall - either way, not for wood) Use heavy duty screws with wide heads (or washers so they don't slip through the holes)

For the other 2 holes, they will be in drywall. So use self-drilling plastic anchors (not molly bolts)
https://www.amazon.com/Drilling-Drywall-Plastic-Anchors-Screws/dp/B09P4JPFB8/ref=sr_1_4?crid=HBH14L538CFS&keywords=heavy%2Bduty%2BSelf%2BDrilling%2BDrywall%2BPlastic%2BAnchors&qid=1659391929&s=hi&sprefix=heavy%2Bdutyself%2Bdrilling%2Bdrywall%2Bplastic%2Banchors%2Ctools%2C160&sr=1-4&th=1

If you do all this correctly, it will work as advertised.
